assumptions: The webhook payload includes a standard Shopify order object with id, name, customer, total_price and financial_status fields.
The shared secret used to generate the X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256 header is available to the integration runtime.
The Slack bot token has the chat:write scope and the target channel ID is known or can be resolved from a channel name.
The integration will reject the webhook if the HMAC-SHA256 signature verification fails.

notes: Must verify HMAC-SHA256 signature from X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256 header using shared secret; reject if invalid.
Raw request body must be used for HMAC verification (do not parse before verification).
Respond with 200 OK within 5 seconds to avoid retries; queue processing asynchronously.
Shopify retries failed deliveries up to 19 times over 48 hours before disabling subscription.
Duplicate deliveries are common; use X-Shopify-Webhook-Id header for idempotency.
Order IDs are 64-bit integers; handle as strings or int64 to avoid precision loss in JavaScript.
No pagination; webhook delivers single order object per POST.
This target represents the HMAC verification step performed on the source webhook request itself; no external HTTP call is made.
Verification is done locally by computing HMAC-SHA256 of raw request body with shared secret and comparing to X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256 header.
If verification fails, connector must return 401 and not proceed to Slack notification.
Shared secret must be available as SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET environment variable.
No pagination; verification operates on single webhook delivery.
Requires chat:write scope on the bot token.
Channel can be specified as channel ID (e.g., C123ABC456) or name; ID is preferred for reliability.
Text field is used as primary message content; blocks or attachments not required for this use case.
No pagination; each webhook triggers exactly one message post.
Rate limited to ~1 message per second per channel; burst limits higher.
Must respond with 200 OK within 5 seconds of receiving Shopify webhook; Slack API call should be fast or queued if slow.
